classifiedFinding.title: _claimRewards underflows and reverts after pauseWithdraw -> unpause -> claim sequence

classification.assetImpact: User's accrued phUSD and stable rewards on their remaining stake become unclaimable (in-motion yield loss). Principal is NOT lost — user can still recover principal via a subsequent full pauseWithdraw, but doing so forfeits all accrued rewards. The user's normal claim/withdraw paths are permanently bricked for any non-full exit.
attackPath: 2. Time elapses; accumulators grow; user accrues rewards.
3. Pauser legitimately pauses the contract (documented operation).
4. User calls pauseWithdraw(partial_amount) — valid input per the function signature.
6. User calls claim() / withdraw(remaining) / stake — all revert with Panic 0x11 because (user.amount * accPerShare) / PRECISION < stale user.debt.
7. Only recovery is another full pauseWithdraw during a future pause, forfeiting all accrued rewards.
classification.likelihood: high — only requires standard pause cycle plus a partial pauseWithdraw (both valid protocol operations); no privileged or unusual inputs
classification.assumptions: Pauser performs at least one pause cycle (documented operational scenario)
classification.externalRequirements: Pause triggered (by trusted pauser or governance)

classifiedFinding.justification: Permanent DoS of normal claim/withdraw for affected user with verified counterexamples (invariant + symbolic). Per C4 special-cases rule, in-motion yield loss is capped at Medium. Principal is recoverable via the documented pauseWithdraw escape (but with forfeiture), so this does not reach High. Function availability is impacted (mutating-path DoS for the user); value leak (rewards forfeited) with stated assumptions (pause cycle).
classifiedFinding.notes: Sanitizer hinted potential-high; classifier downgrades to Medium because principal is not at risk (user retains pauseWithdraw escape) and the yield is in-motion/unmatured. Verified counterexamples make this a high-quality Medium with strong PoC.
